objective: Review the capability registry commit on release/0.3.1/feat/capabilities in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-cap against the merge-ready bar.
scope: Range: git -C /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-cap diff 5d2bed8..HEAD (one commit). The registry is packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts; form detection is setup/form.ts; setup/doctor/TUI wiring in setup/ and cli/setup.ts; pi/tools.ts; integrations/pi/src/agents.ts.

Maintainer requirements (verbatim): "everything should be modular and easily upgradeable btw" and "btw we shall support both headless use and normal use, that's the point of capabilities, to modularly support systems". Scope: move the seven existing optional capabilities onto the registry with unchanged behavior and defaults; headless/normal detection with an override; a flag and a TUI row per capability; doctor health per capability; no version outside config/pi-packages.json; no new 0.3.1 capabilities.

Behavior changes the writer reported, judge each: headless machines (CI, cloud session, Linux without a display) no longer get computer-use and setup removes a listed package; doctor lines renamed (pi features -> pi base packages, pi form, pi capability <name>); the setup screen now opens whenever Pi is in use and pi.enable is on (skipped for --undo, cloud sessions and capability flags), not only when T3 has work; setup --undo leaves capability choices in config; a user-level computerUse false beats a project-level on.

Check that a 0.3.0 config decodes and behaves the same, that the setup screen never opens without a TTY or in scripted runs, that headless detection cannot misfire on a normal desktop (Windows, macOS, Wayland), Effect and Schema rules from .claude/CLAUDE.md, JSDoc, and that tests would fail without the change. Run the built-in /code-review on the range and classify its findings.
constraints: Do not check out other commits in any checkout and make no edits.
Report in under 400 words; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking with file and line.

criteria.text: Registry-driven behavior is correct and existing defaults and 0.3.0 configs behave unchanged except the stated changes
Headless detection and the setup screen trigger are safe on every supported platform and in non-interactive runs
Tests cover the change and fail without it
